parts.name: GMKtec NucBox K6, Ryzen 7 7840HS
parts.storage: 2x M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 NVMe; vendor states up to 4TB total expansion
parts.software_stack: x86-64 Linux/Windows; llama.cpp CPU; Vulkan/ROCm paths where supported by the exact runtime and driver
parts.plain_language: A documented 7840HS reference node with dual 2.5GbE, dual NVMe and replaceable DDR5. It is useful as a used-market efficiency baseline, but the 120W adapter rating is only an input-capacity specification and is not treated as inference power.
parts.source_notes: GMKtec documents Ryzen 7 7840HS, Radeon 780M, two DDR5-5600 SO-DIMM slots with 64GB maximum, dual M.2 PCIe 4.0 storage, dual 2.5GbE and Linux support. The official store currently shows the K6 sold out; live secondary-market price is required.

parts.name: Beelink SER8, Ryzen 7 8845HS
parts.storage: 2x M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 x4; vendor states up to 8TB total
parts.expandability: dual SO-DIMM, dual NVMe, full-featured USB4
parts.software_stack: x86-64 Linux/Windows; llama.cpp CPU; Vulkan/ROCm paths where supported by the exact runtime and driver
parts.plain_language: The SER8 is a useful 8845HS reference because Beelink documents unusually high DDR5 capacity, dual NVMe and compact cooling. The vendor's 256GB memory claim is retained as board-level support evidence, while exact DIMM compatibility should still be validated before a large-memory purchase.
parts.source_notes: Beelink documents Ryzen 7 8845HS, Radeon 780M, dual DDR5-5600 SO-DIMM with a stated 256GB maximum, dual M.2 PCIe 4.0 x4, 2.5GbE and USB4. Adapter wattage and the vendor's 65W processor mode are not complete-node inference-power measurements.

parts.name: MINISFORUM UM890 Pro, Ryzen 9 8945HS
parts.expandability: dual SO-DIMM, dual NVMe, 2x USB4, OCuLink PCIe 4.0 x4
parts.software_stack: x86-64 Linux/Windows; llama.cpp CPU; Vulkan/ROCm paths where supported; OCuLink allows a discrete-GPU expansion path
parts.plain_language: A stronger 8945HS cluster/reference node with 96GB board-verified DDR5 support, dual 2.5GbE and OCuLink. It is especially useful when the same compact host may later be paired with an external GPU without replacing the node.
parts.source_notes: MINISFORUM documents Ryzen 9 8945HS, Radeon 780M, two DDR5-5600 SO-DIMM slots up to 96GB, two PCIe 4.0 NVMe slots, dual 2.5GbE, dual USB4 and OCuLink. The vendor advertises high processor power modes, but no complete-node inference wattage is inferred.

parts.name: MINISFORUM AI X1 Pro, Ryzen AI 9 HX 370
parts.expandability: dual SO-DIMM, triple NVMe, 2x USB4, OCuLink PCIe 4.0 x4
parts.software_stack: x86-64 Linux/Windows; llama.cpp CPU/Vulkan; ROCm where supported; Ryzen AI NPU is a specialist path and is not treated as equivalent to LLM GPU throughput
parts.plain_language: This is a high-end HX370 reference with Radeon 890M, three NVMe slots, dual 2.5GbE and OCuLink. The formal MINISFORUM specification table says 96GB maximum DDR5 even though another marketing section says 128GB, so the catalog keeps the conservative 96GB figure until the vendor reconciles the page.
parts.source_notes: MINISFORUM documents Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, Radeon 890M, triple M.2, dual 2.5GbE, Wi-Fi 7, dual USB4 and OCuLink. The page contains conflicting 128GB and 96GB memory claims; this record uses the formal product-specification table's 96GB maximum. Marketing TOPS are not converted to tokens/sec.

parts.name: Radxa ROCK 5B+, RK3588, 32GB LPDDR5
parts.network: 2.5GbE with optional PoE HAT; onboard Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.2
parts.storage: onboard eMMC options plus microSD; 2x M.2 M-key PCIe 3.0 x2 NVMe connectors
parts.expandability: dual NVMe, M.2 B-key cellular, GPIO and camera/display interfaces
parts.software_stack: Debian/Radxa OS/Armbian-class Linux; llama.cpp CPU/Vulkan community paths; RKNN NPU for supported specialist models
parts.plain_language: ROCK 5B+ adds another official 32GB RK3588 option with LPDDR5, 2.5GbE and two NVMe connectors. It is a compact memory-dense worker candidate, but exact llama.cpp/Vulkan throughput and complete-board power still require exact-image/runtime measurements.
parts.source_notes: Radxa documents RK3588, 32GB LPDDR5, Mali-G610 Vulkan 1.2, 6-TOPS NPU, 2.5GbE, onboard Wi-Fi 6 and two PCIe 3.0 x2 M.2 NVMe connectors. USB-C PD capabilities are input specifications, not measured inference power.

parts.name: Radxa ROCK 4D, RK3576, 16GB LPDDR5
parts.network: Gigabit Ethernet with optional PoE; Wi-Fi 6; Bluetooth 5.4
parts.expandability: PCIe 2.1 x1 over FPC, GPIO, UFS/eMMC, camera/display interfaces
parts.software_stack: Debian Linux/Android/Yocto/Buildroot; llama.cpp CPU/Vulkan experimentation; RKNN NPU for supported specialist models
parts.plain_language: ROCK 4D is the lower-cost/lower-complexity RK3576 branch of the catalog. The 16GB variant is large enough for useful small-model experiments and gives the project a newer Rockchip comparison below RK3588, without pretending the 6-TOPS NPU is a general LLM score.
parts.source_notes: Radxa documents RK3576, 16GB LPDDR5, Mali-G52, 6-TOPS NPU, Gigabit Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6, UFS/eMMC expansion and Debian Linux support. No board-power number is inferred from its USB-C or PoE input options.

parts.name: Orange Pi 5, RK3588S, 32GB LPDDR4X
parts.storage: microSD, 16MB QSPI and M.2 M-key NVMe
parts.software_stack: Orange Pi OS/Ubuntu/Debian/Android; llama.cpp CPU/Vulkan community paths; Rockchip NPU for supported specialist models
parts.plain_language: The plain Orange Pi 5 32GB is a smaller, simpler 32GB RK3588S node than the existing 5 Plus. It trades the Plus model's richer networking for a compact footprint while keeping enough RAM to be genuinely useful for local-model capacity experiments.
parts.source_notes: Orange Pi documents an exact 32GB LPDDR4X variant with RK3588S, Mali-G610 Vulkan 1.2, 6-TOPS NPU, Gigabit Ethernet, M.2 NVMe and Linux/Android support. Its 5V/4A input requirement is not recorded as measured inference power.
